paragraphs: We are a biotechnology company committed to establishing the leading, fully integrated platform for precision genetic medicines. Our vision is to provide life-long cures to patients suffering from serious diseases. To achieve this vision, we have assembled a platform that includes a suite of gene editing and delivery technologies as well as internal manufacturing capabilities.

Our suite of gene editing technologies is anchored by our proprietary base editing technology, which potentially enables a differentiated class of precision genetic medicines that target a single base in the genome without making a double-stranded break in the DNA. This approach uses a chemical reaction designed to create precise, predictable and efficient genetic outcomes at the targeted sequence. Our proprietary base editors have two principal components: (i) a clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats, or CRISPR, protein, bound to a guide RNA, that leverages the established DNA-targeting ability of CRISPR, but is modified to not cause a double-stranded break, and (ii) a base editing enzyme, such as a deaminase, which carries out the desired chemical modification of the target DNA base. We believe this design contributes to a more precise and efficient edit compared to traditional gene editing methods, with the potential to dramatically increase the impact of gene editing. We are also pursuing a suite of delivery modalities, including both ex vivo and in vivo approaches, depending on tissue type. The elegance of the base editing approach, combined with a tissue specific delivery modality, provides the basis for a targeted, efficient, precise, and highly versatile gene editing system that is designed to be capable of gene correction, gene silencing, gene activation, gene modification, and/or multiplex editing of several genes simultaneously.

Our goal is to advance a broad, diversified portfolio of base editing programs against distinct, genetically validated editing targets, as well as an innovative, platform business model that will expand the reach of our programs to more patients. Overall, we are seeking to build the leading integrated platform for precision genetic medicine, which may have broad therapeutic applicability and the potential to transform the field of precision genetic medicines.

We are currently prioritizing the lead programs in our hematology and genetic disease portfolios, each of which have the potential to provide differentiated therapies for significant patient populations with high unmet medical need:

• Ristoglogene autogetemcel, or risto-cel (formerly known as BEAM-101), is a patient-specific, autologous hematopoietic stem cell, or HSC, investigational therapy designed to offer a potentially best-in-class profile, incorporating base edits that are intended to alleviate the effects of sickle cell disease by increasing fetal hemoglobin, which is expected to increase functional hemoglobin production and, in the case of sickle cell disease, inhibit hemoglobin S polymerization. In December 2025, we announced additional positive data from our Phase 1/2 clinical trial of risto-cel, which we refer to as the BEACON trial. We expect to submit a biologics license application, or BLA, for risto-cel as early as year-end 2026.

• BEAM-302 is a liver-targeting lipid nanoparticle, or LNP, formulation of base editing reagents designed to offer a one-time treatment to correct the E342K point mutation (PiZZ genotype), which is most commonly responsible for severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, or AATD. We have reached alignment with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, on a potential accelerated approval pathway for BEAM-302 based on alpha-1 antitrypsin biomarkers evaluated over 12 months. To support a future BLA submission, we anticipate enrolling approximately 50 additional patients to be treated with the selected optimal biological dose of BEAM-302 in an expansion of the ongoing Phase 1/2 clinical trial. We expect to report updated data from the trial and next steps for pivotal development by the end of the first quarter of 2026.
We are also continuing to advance our other hematology and genetic diseases programs:

• We continue to make significant investments in developing targeted LNPs for the in vivo delivery of gene editing payloads to HSCs. Based on recent advancements in this technology, we are now prioritizing in vivo delivery for our next wave approach to treating sickle cell disease. We have identified multiple targeted LNPs that have the potential for HSC delivery and are currently engaged in lead optimization. We are also continuing development of our proprietary ESCAPE platform, a technology to potentially enable non-genotoxic treatment strategies that can be delivered either ex vivo or in vivo, including as part of any future in vivo program for sickle cell disease. The ongoing Phase 1 healthy volunteer clinical trial of BEAM-103, an anti-CD117 monoclonal antibody that enables ESCAPE, is expected to complete dosing in the first half of 2026.

• BEAM-304 is a newly announced liver-targeting LNP formulation of base editing reagents designed to correct disease-causing mutations responsible for phenylketonuria, or PKU. Initial clinical development will focus on base editors addressing the two most prevalent variants found in nearly half of patients with PKU, with ongoing research efforts to address additional pathogenic mutations. In 2026, we plan to submit a regulatory application to initiate a Phase 1/2 dose-escalation clinical trial of BEAM-304 in PKU patients with the R408W mutation.

• BEAM-301 is a liver-targeting LNP formulation of base editing reagents designed to correct the R83C mutation, the most prevalent disease-causing mutation for, and the mutation which results in the most severe form of, glycogen storage disease type 1a, or GSDIa. We are evaluating BEAM-301 in a Phase 1/2 clinical trial, and expect to report initial clinical data in 2026.

Gene editing works by disrupting, inserting, or modifying genes in the natural context of the genome. Most established gene editing methods rely on a class of enzymes, called nucleases, to make a double-stranded break in the DNA at a targeted location. Nuclease editors have several significant limitations.

First, there is a lack of predictability in genetic outcomes when altering gene sequences with nucleases. Nuclease editors can be effective if the desired outcome is to knock out or switch off the whole gene, but do not allow for precise control of the specific genetic outcome at the target site and its effects may vary from individual to individual.

Second, there are potential toxicities associated with double-stranded breaks, such as activating the cell death response and/or genomic instability. In addition, if the double-stranded break occurs in the wrong place, the break can also lead to unwanted gene disruptions. Multiple edits using double-stranded breaks can compound this issue and lead to large-scale genomic translocations and rearrangements, potentially limiting the applicability of nuclease-based approaches in multiplex editing.

Third, while gene disruption with nucleases is efficient, making specific sequence changes to correct or modify genes remains largely inefficient. It also requires the simultaneous delivery of an additional DNA template containing the desired, corrected gene sequence, which needs to be positioned at the precise location where the double-stranded break has occurred. The requirement of an additional DNA template significantly increases the complexity of delivery.

paragraphs: You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below together with all of the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our consolidated financial statements and related notes appearing at the end of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, in evaluating our company. If any of the events or developments described below were to occur, our business, prospects, operating results and financial condition could suffer materially, and the trading price of our common stock could decline. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial may also adversely affect our business.

Since inception, we have incurred significant operating losses. Our net loss was $80.0 million, $376.7 million and $132.5 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $1.6 billion. We have financed our operations primarily through private placements of our preferred stock, proceeds from sales of our common stock, collaboration revenue and our credit facility with Sixth Street Lending Partners. We have devoted substantially all of our efforts to research and development. We expect to continue to incur significant expenses and increasing operating losses for the foreseeable future. The net losses we incur may fluctuate significantly from quarter to quarter. We anticipate that our expenses will increase substantially if and as we:
• advance clinical trials of our product candidates;
• continue our research programs and our preclinical development of other product candidates from our research programs;
• seek to identify additional research programs and additional product candidates;
• initiate preclinical testing and clinical trials for any other product candidates we identify and develop;

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and the related notes to those statements included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. In addition to historical financial information, the following discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements that involve risks, uncertainties and assumptions. Some of the numbers included herein have been rounded for the convenience of presentation. Our actual results may differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of many factors, including those discussed under Item 1A, Risk factors, in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Information pertaining to fiscal year 2023 was included in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 on pages 111 through 123 under Part II, Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Position and Results of Operations," which was filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") on February 25, 2025.

Our vision is to provide life-long cures to patients suffering from serious diseases. To achieve this vision, we have assembled a platform that includes a suite of gene editing and delivery technologies as well as internal manufacturing capabilities.

This approach uses a chemical reaction designed to create precise, predictable and efficient genetic outcomes at the targeted sequence. Our proprietary base editors have two principal components: (i) a clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats, or CRISPR, protein, bound to a guide RNA, that leverages the established DNA-targeting ability of CRISPR, but is modified to not cause a double-stranded break, and (ii) a base editing enzyme, such as a deaminase, which carries out the desired chemical modification of the target DNA base. We believe this design contributes to a more precise and efficient edit compared to traditional gene editing methods, with the potential to dramatically increase the impact of gene editing. We are also pursuing a suite of delivery modalities, including both ex vivo and in vivo approaches, depending on tissue type. The elegance of the base editing approach, combined with a tissue specific delivery modality, provides the basis for a targeted, efficient, precise, and highly versatile gene editing system that is designed to be capable of gene correction, gene silencing, gene activation, gene modification, and/or multiplex editing of several genes simultaneously.

Our goal is to advance a broad, diversified portfolio of base editing programs against distinct, genetically validated editing targets, as well as an innovative, platform business model that will expand the reach of our programs to more patients. Overall, we are seeking to build the leading integrated platform for precision genetic medicine, which may have broad therapeutic applicability and the potential to transform the field of precision genetic medicines.

We are pursuing a long-term, staged development strategy for our base editing approach to treat hematological diseases, such as sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. Our initial wave consists of ex vivo programs in which hematopoietic stem cells, or HSCs, are collected from a patient, edited using electroporation, and then infused back into the patient following a conditioning regimen, such as treatment with busulfan, the standard of care in HSC transplantation, or HSCTs, today. Once reinfused, the HSCs begin repopulating a portion of the bone marrow in a process known as engraftment. The engrafted, edited HSCs give rise to progenitor cell types with the corrected gene sequences. We are deploying this ex vivo approach in our risto-cel program. We are also pursuing a next wave of in vivo base editing with delivery directly into HSCs of patients via LNPs. We believe this multi-wave strategy can maximize the potential applicability of our sickle cell disease programs to patients as well as create a platform for the treatment of many other severe genetic blood disorders.

We are using base editing to pursue the development of risto-cel for the treatment of sickle cell disease. Risto-cel is a patient-specific, autologous HSC investigational therapy designed to offer a potentially best-in-class profile, incorporating base edits that are intended to mimic single nucleotide polymorphisms seen in individuals with hereditary persistence of fetal hemoglobin, or HbF.

Risto-cel aims to alleviate the effects of sickle cell disease by increasing HbF, which is expected to increase functional hemoglobin production and, in the case of sickle cell disease, inhibit hemoglobins S, or HbS, polymerization.

We are conducting a Phase 1/2 clinical trial designed to assess the safety and efficacy of risto-cel for the treatment of sickle cell disease, which we refer to as our BEACON trial. The BEACON trial includes approximately 50 adults and adolescents with severe sickle cell disease who have received prior treatment with at least one disease-modifying agent with inadequate response or intolerance. Following mobilization, conditioning and treatment with risto-cel, patients are assessed for safety and tolerability, with safety endpoints including neutrophil and platelet engraftment. Patients are also assessed for efficacy, with efficacy endpoints including the change from baseline in severe vaso-occlusive events, transfusion requirements, HbF levels, and quality of life assessments. The adult and adolescent enrollment for BEACON is complete, and manufacturing of all doses was completed as of

December 2025. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or the FDA, has granted orphan drug designation and regenerative medicine advanced therapy designation to risto-cel. Risto-cel has also been accepted into the FDA's Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls Development and Readiness pilot program.

In December 2025, we presented updated data from the BEACON trial at the American Society of Hematology 2025 Annual Meeting, or ASH. The presentation contained preliminary data as of August 6, 2025, from 31 patients in the trial, with follow up ranging from 0.3 to 20.4 months. The presentation data included the following:

• Patients achieved mean HbF levels above 60% and a mean durable reduction in corresponding HbS below 40%. A pancellular distribution of HbF, reflecting expression across most of the circulating red blood cells, was observed, with mean per-cell HbF levels maintained above the sickling threshold throughout follow-up. Durable, high editing efficiency was observed in peripheral blood and bone marrow following treatment with risto-cel. Mean peripheral blood editing was 67.4% at Month 6 and 72.8% by Month 12

• Patients required a median of one (range: 1-5) stem cell collection cycle, comprising a median of three (range: 1–13) total collection days for the risto-cel manufacturing process and back-up cell collection. The median time to neutrophil engraftment was 17.5 days (range: 12-30), with a median duration of severe neutropenia of seven days (range: 1-17). The median time to platelet engraftment was 19 days (range: 11-53). In addition, 29% of patients did not require any platelet transfusions following risto-cel treatment.

• Total Hb levels increased rapidly with all patients experiencing resolution of anemia after elimination of the transfused blood. Key markers of hemolysis, including indirect bilirubin, haptoglobin, lactate dehydrogenase, and reticulocytes, normalized or improved in all patients following risto-cel treatment. Erythropoietin levels also trended toward normal, indicating significant improvement in oxygen delivery to tissues. Sickling parameters all decreased in the blood following risto-cel treatment to levels comparable to those seen in individuals with sickle cell trait.

paragraphs: 本公司為一生物科技公司，致力於建立領先的、完全整合的精準遺傳藥物平台。我們的願景是為罹患嚴重疾病的患者提供終身治癒方案。為達成此願景，我們已組建一個包含基因編輯與遞送技術組合以及內部製造能力的平台。

我們的基因編輯技術組合以我們專有的鹼基編輯技術為核心，該技術潛在可提供一種差異化的精準遺傳藥物，針對基因組中單一鹼基進行作用，而不造成雙鏈DNA斷裂。此方法使用化學反應，設計用以在目標序列中產生精確、可預測且高效的遺傳結果。我們專有的鹼基編輯器包含兩個主要零組件：(i) 一組與引導RNA結合的聚類定間隔短迴文重複序列，或稱為CRISPR蛋白，利用CRISPR已建立的DNA目標定位能力，但經過修改以避免造成雙鏈斷裂；(ii) 一種鹼基編輯酶，例如脫氨酶，執行目標DNA鹼基的所需化學修飾。我們認為此設計可帶來較傳統基因編輯方法更精確且高效的編輯，潛在可大幅提高基因編輯的影響力。我們同時也在進行一系列遞送模式的開發，包括根據組織類型的體外與體內方法。鹼基編輯方法的優雅特性，結合組織特定的遞送模式，為一種具針對性、高效能、精確且高度靈活的基因編輯系統奠定基礎，此係統設計可實現基因修復、基因沉默、基因活化、基因修飾，以及/或同時進行多個基因的多重編輯。
我們的目標是推進一系列廣泛且多元化的鹼基編輯計畫，針對不同的、已驗證的遺傳編輯目標，同時建立創新、平台化的商業模式，以擴展我們計畫的覆蓋範圍至更多患者。總體而言，我們致力於建立領先的整合精準遺傳藥物平台，此平台可能具有廣泛的治療應用潛力，並潛在可改變精準遺傳藥物領域。
目前，我們優先推動我們血液學與遺傳疾病計畫中的領先計畫，每個計畫均有潛力為具有高度未滿足醫療需求的大量患者提供差異化的治療方案：

• Ristoglogene autogetemcel，或稱risto-cel（先前稱為BEAM-101），為一種個別患者特定的自體造血幹細胞，或HSC，研究性治療，設計提供潛在最佳等級的治療方案，包含鹼基編輯，旨在緩解貧血細胞疾病（sickle cell disease）的影響，透過增加胎兒血紅蛋白，預期可提高功能性血紅蛋白的產生，並在貧血細胞疾病的情況下，抑制血紅蛋白S的聚合。2025年12月，我們宣佈了有關risto-cel的Phase 1/2臨牀試驗的更多正面數據，我們稱為BEACON試驗。我們預期在2026年底前提交生物製品許可申請，或BLA，以核准risto-cel。

• BEAM-302為一種針對肝臟的脂質奈米粒子，或LNP，配方的鹼基編輯試劑，設計提供一次性治療以修正E342K點變異（PiZZ基因型），此變異為嚴重α-1抗胰蛋白酶缺乏症，或AATD，最常見的原因。我們已與美國食品藥物管理局，或FDA，達成共識，針對BEAM-302的潛在加速核准途徑，基於在12個月內評估的α-1抗胰蛋白酶生物指標。為支持未來BLA申請，我們預期招募約50名額外患者，接受選定的最佳生物劑量的BEAM-302治療，作為現有Phase 1/2臨牀試驗的擴展。我們預期在2026年第一季末報告試驗的更新數據與未來關鍵發展的下一步驟。
我們同時也在持續推進其他血液學與遺傳疾病計畫：

• 我們持續在開發針對體內遞送基因編輯載具至HSC的專屬LNP。根據此技術最近的進展，我們現在優先考慮體內遞送作為治療貧血細胞疾病的下一階段方法。我們已鑑定多種具備HSC遞送潛力的專屬LNP，並目前正進行主要優化。我們同時持續開發我們專有的ESCAPE平台，一種技術，潛在可實現非基因毒性的治療策略，可透過體外或體內方式遞送，包括作為未來體內計畫中貧血細胞疾病的任何應用。現行的Phase 1健康志工臨牀試驗BEAM-103，一種反CD117單株抗體，可啟動ESCAPE，預期在2026年上半年完成劑量給予。

• BEAM-304 是一種新近宣佈的針對肝臟的 LNP 零組件，用於修正導致苯酮尿症（phenylketonuria，簡稱 PKU）的致病變異，初始臨牀開發將聚焦於修正 PKU 患者中近一半患者所見的兩種最常見變異，並持續進行研究以修正其他致病變異。預計在 2026 年，本公司將提交一個監管申請，以啟動針對具 R408W 變異的 PKU 患者 BEAM-304 的 Phase 1/2 劑量遞增臨牀試驗。
• BEAM-301 是一種針對肝臟的 LNP 零組件，用於修正 R83C 變異，這是導致 Glycogen Storage Disease Type 1a（簡稱 GSDIa）的最常見致病變異，且會導致最嚴重形式的 GSDIa。本公司正在評估 BEAM-301 在 Phase 1/2 臨牀試驗中的表現，預計在 2026 年報告初步臨牀數據。
基因編輯透過幹擾、插入或修改基因在基因組中的自然情境來進行。大多數已建立的基因編輯方法依賴一類稱為核酸酶的酵素，在 DNA 的目標位置產生雙股斷裂。核酸酶編輯器有幾個顯著的限制。
首先，當使用核酸酶改變基因序列時，遺傳結果的可預測性不足。核酸酶編輯器如果目標是敲除或關閉整個基因，可能有效，但無法對目標位點的特定遺傳結果進行精確控制，其效果可能因個體而異。
其次，雙股斷裂可能導致潛在毒性，例如啟動細胞死亡反應和/或基因組不穩定性。此外，如果雙股斷裂發生在錯誤的位置，斷裂也可能導致不想要的基因幹擾。使用雙股斷裂進行多個編輯會加劇此問題，導致大規模的基因組轉位和重組，這可能會限制核酸酶基於方法在多重編輯中的應用。
第三，雖然使用核酸酶進行基因幹擾效率較高，但要進行特定序列變更以修正或修改基因仍屬低效。這也需要同時遞送一個包含所需修正基因序列的額外 DNA 模板，並將其精確定位在雙股斷裂發生的位置。需要額外 DNA 模板的條件顯著增加了遞送的複雜性。

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與我們的合併財務報表及相關附註說明一併閱讀，這些財務報表及附註說明包含於本年度報表 10-K 的其他部分。除了歷史財務資訊外，以下討論與分析包含許多前瞻性陳述，這些陳述涉及風險、不確定性與假設。部分 herein 所包含的數字為方便呈現而四捨五入。我們的實際結果可能與這些前瞻性陳述中預期的結果有重大差異，原因可能包括那些在本年度報表 10-K 的第 1A 項「風險因素」中討論的多種因素。
有關財務年度 2023 年的資訊，已包含於我們 2024 年 12 月 31 日為結算日的年度報表 10-K，頁碼 111 至 123，位於第二部分，第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析」，該部分已於 2025 年 2 月 25 日提交至證券交易委員會（Securities and Exchange Commission，簡稱 SEC）。
我們是一家生物科技公司，致力於建立領先的、完全整合的精準遺傳藥物平台。我們的願景是為患有嚴重疾病的患者提供終身治癒方案。為實現此願景，我們已組建了一個包含基因編輯與遞送技術組合以及內部製造能力的平台。

我們的基因編輯技術組合以我們專有的鹼基編輯技術為核心，這種技術潛在地能提供一種差異化的精準遺傳藥物，針對基因組中單一鹼基進行作用，而不會造成雙鏈 DNA 的斷裂。這種方法使用化學反應，設計用以在目標序列中產生精確、可預測且高效的遺傳結果。我們專有的鹼基編輯器包含兩個主要零組件：(i) 一個與引導 RNA 綁定的 clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats，或 CRISPR 蛋白，利用 CRISPR 已建立的 DNA 對目標能力，但經過修改以避免造成雙鏈斷裂；以及 (ii) 一個鹼基編輯酶，如脫氨酶，執行目標 DNA 鹼基的所需化學修飾。我們認為這種設計相比傳統基因編輯方法能提供更精確且高效的編輯，潛在地大幅提高基因編輯的影響力。我們也在追蹤一系列遞送方式，包括根據組織類型而採用的 ex vivo 與 in vivo 方式。鹼基編輯方法的優雅性，結合組織特定的遞送方式，為一種針對性、高效、精確且高度靈活的基因編輯系統奠定了基礎，這種系統設計用以實現基因修復、基因沉默、基因活化、基因修飾，以及/或同時進行多個基因的多重編輯。
我們的目標是推進一系列廣泛且多樣化的鹼基編輯計畫，針對不同的、經過遺傳驗證的編輯目標，同時建立一個創新、平台型的商業模式，以擴展我們計畫的覆蓋範圍，惠及更多患者。總體而言，我們致力於建立領先的整合平台，用以提供精準遺傳藥物，這種平台可能具有廣泛的治療應用潛力，並有潛力改變精準遺傳藥物的領域。

我們正在追蹤一個長期、分階段的開發策略，用以透過鹼基編輯方法治療血液疾病，例如鐮狀細胞疾病與 beta-地中海貧血。我們的第一階段包括 ex vivo 計畫，其中造血幹細胞，或 HSCs，會從患者身上收集，透過電穿孔進行編輯，然後在完成條件性治療方案，例如使用 busulfan 的治療，這是目前 HSC 移植的標準療法，或 HSCTs 之後，再將其回輸至患者體內。一旦回輸，HSCs 開始在骨髓中重新生成一部分，這個過程稱為植入。植入並經過編輯的 HSCs 會產生具有正確基因序列的前體細胞類型。我們正在我們的 risto-cel 計畫中部署這種 ex vivo 方式。我們也在追蹤下一階段的 in vivo 鹼基編輯，透過 LNPs 直接遞送至患者的 HSCs。我們認為這種多階段策略可以最大化我們的鐮狀細胞疾病計畫對患者的應用潛力，同時建立一個治療許多其他嚴重遺傳血液疾病的平台。
我們正在使用鹼基編輯來開發 risto-cel，用以治療鐮狀細胞疾病。Risto-cel 是一種針對患者個別的、自體的 HSC 研究性治療，設計用以提供一種潛在的最優等型的特性，包含鹼基編輯，旨在模擬在具有遺傳性胎兒血紅蛋白持續存在，或 HbF 的個體中觀察到的單一核苷酸多態性。
Risto-cel 的目標是透過增加 HbF 來緩解鐮狀細胞疾病的影響，這被預期會增加功能性血紅蛋白的產生，而在鐮狀細胞疾病的情況下，會抑制血紅蛋白 S，或 HbS 的聚合。

我們正在進行一項 Phase 1/2 臨牀試驗，旨在評估 risto-cel 對治療鐮狀細胞貧血症的安全性與有效性，我們稱此為 BEACON 試驗。BEACON 試驗包括約 50 名患有嚴重鐮狀細胞貧血症的成人與青少年患者，這些患者曾接受過至少一種疾病修正藥物治療但反應不足或無法耐受。在動員、條件化處理及接受 risto-cel 治療後，患者會被評估其安全性與耐受性，安全性評估指標包括中性粒細胞與血小板植入。患者也會被評估其有效性，有效性評估指標包括從基線值變化嚴重血管閉塞事件、輸血需求、HbF 水準與生活品質評估。BEACON 試驗的成人與青少年入組已經完成，所有劑量的製造於
2025 年 12 月完成。美國食品藥物管理局，或稱 FDA，已授予 risto-cel 罕見疾病藥物指定與再生醫學先進療法指定。risto-cel 也已獲 FDA 的化學、製造與管制開發與準備試點計畫接受。
2025 年 12 月，我們在美國血液學會 2025 年年會，或稱 ASH，展示 BEACON 試驗的更新資料。展示內容包含截至 2025 年 8 月 6 日的初步資料，來自試驗中的 31 名患者，追蹤時間範圍為 0.3 至 20.4 個月。展示資料包含以下內容：
• 患者達成平均 HbF 水準超過 60%，且平均持續降低的 HbS 水準低於 40%。觀察到 HbF 的全細胞分佈，反映在大多數循環紅血球中表現，平均每個細胞 HbF 水準維持在鐮狀細胞危機閾值之上，追蹤期間持續穩定。在接受 risto-cel 治療後，外周血與骨髓中觀察到持續且高效率的編輯效果。治療後第六個月的平均外周血編輯為 67.4%，至第十二個月時為 72.8%

• 患者平均需要一個（範圍：1-5）幹細胞收集週期，包含 risto-cel 製造過程的平均總收集天數為三個（範圍：1–13）以及備用細胞收集。中性粒細胞植入的中位數時間為 17.5 天（範圍：12-30），嚴重中性粒細胞減少的中位數持續時間為七天（範圍：1-17）。血小板植入的中位數時間為 19 天（範圍：11-53）。此外，29% 的患者在接受 risto-cel 治療後不需要任何血小板輸注。
• 所有患者的總 Hb 水準迅速增加，所有患者在去除輸血血液後都恢復了血紅素缺乏症。血紅素分解的關鍵指標，包括間接膽紅素、血漿鐵蛋白、乳酸脫氫酶與網織紅血球，在接受 risto-cel 治療後都恢復正常或改善。促紅血球生成素水準也趨近正常，顯示組織氧氣供應有顯著改善。在接受 risto-cel 治療後，血液中的鐮狀細胞參數都降低至與具有鐮狀細胞特質者所見的水平相當。

headings: 與本公司財務狀況相關之風險及對額外資金之需求
自設立以來，本公司已產生重大虧損。本公司預期在可預見之未來將持續產生虧損，並可能永遠無法達成或維持獲利。
籌措額外資金可能導致股東持股稀釋、限制本公司營運，或要求本公司放棄智慧財產權或可能開發之產品候選技術之權利。
本公司營運歷史較短，可能使您難以評估本公司迄今之營運成效，並評估本公司未來之生存能力。
本公司從未自產品銷售中產生收入，並可能永遠無法成為獲利之公司。
本公司未來利用淨營業虧損結轉及某些其他稅務屬性之能力可能受到限制。
與發現、開發及商業化相關之風險
若本公司在臨牀試驗中遭遇患者入組或治療之延誤或困難，本公司取得必要監管機構核准之時程可能延後或無法取得
paragraphs: 您應仔細審閱下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並與本年度10-K形式年度報告中包含的所有其他資訊，包括我們的合併財務報表及相關附註，共同評估本公司。如果下列所描述的任何事件或發展發生，將可能對我們的業務、前景、營運結果與財務狀況造成重大影響，並導致我們普通股的交易價格下跌。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為不重要，也可能對我們的業務造成不利影響。

自設立以來，我們已產生顯著的營運虧損。我們的淨虧損為 80.0 百萬美元、376.7 百萬美元及 132.5 百萬美元，分別為 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日所終結之會計年度。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們累計虧損為 1.6 十億美元。我們主要透過私募發行本公司優先股、銷售本公司普通股所得金額、合作收入及與 Sixth Street Lending Partners 之信用融資協議來支應營運。我們已將 substantially all 之努力投入研究與開發。我們預期將持續產生顯著費用及增加營運虧損，於可預見之未來。我們所產生之淨虧損可能自季度至季度間大幅波動。我們預期若並如我們：
• 推進我們產品候選品的臨牀試驗；
• 繼續我們的研究計畫與來自我們研究計畫的其他產品候選品的前期臨牀開發；
• 尋求識別額外的研究計畫與額外的產品候選品；
• 啟動我們所識別與開發的任何其他產品候選品的前期臨牀測試與臨牀試驗；
